newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West spot power prices steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West spot power prices steady to higher.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the U.S. Mid-West were mostly steady for weekend delivery with some higher prices for Monday business due to fall maintenance outages at coal and nuclear power plants, industry sources said.
"There seems to be enough units out for maintenance next week that if we were to lose any for repairs we could see some tight supply," said one power marketer.

The Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP) and Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) regions held fairly steady for Monday delivery however, with little spot business being done due to lackluster demand and some line-loading out of MAPP, the sources said.
On-peak next day power for a 16-hour block in MAPP was talked steady in the $12.00-15.50 range for weekend and Monday delivery, the brokers and marketers said.
Off-peak MAPP power was pegged steady in the $7.50-9.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, the sources said.
On-peak prices in the MAIN region for weekend and Monday delivery were said to be holding in the $16.50-19.50 per MWh range.
Off-peak MAIN power was said to be steady in the $9.50-11.00 per MWh range, the sources said.
October MAIN was assessed over a wide range of $15.50-18.50 per MWh.

In the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR), peak power prices for weekend delivery were quoted steady at $15.00-16.00, while Monday was talked higher at $17.00-20.00, the sources said.
Off peak ECAR was said to be unchanged in the $11.50-14.00 per MWh range.
October ECAR was talked in the $16.50-17.50 range, the sources said.

In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), on-peak power for Friday delivery in the north area was assessed steady in the $13.00-15.00 range for the weekend, but assessed higher at $15.00-16.00 for Monday delivery.
Off-peak was pegged at $10.00-11.00 per MWh.
In the south of SPP, power was pegged steady at $16.75-17.75 through the weekend and up to $17.75-18.25 for Monday.
Off peak was assessed near $12.00, the sources said.
October SPP was assessed steady in the $15.50-17.50 area.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
